title: Cystometry in Awake Rats
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bakjicun

steps.title: Prepare bladder cannula
steps.instruction: Prepare the bladder cannula at least 24–48 h before surgery. Cut ~25 cm PVC tubing for males (≈20 cm for females) and ~2 cm PE tubing. Flare the PE tubing end over an open flame, cut the flared tip to 0.5–1 cm, and insert the non‑flared end 2–3 mm into the PVC tubing; secure with superglue. Cut 0.5–1 cm silastic tubing, glue it to the exteriorised end of the cannula, leaving a 5 cm overhang to form the collar.

substeps.instruction: Cut PVC tubing to required length (≈25 cm male, ≈20 cm female)
Flare PE tubing end over flame and trim to 0.5–1 cm
Insert PE tubing 2–3 mm into PVC tubing and secure with superglue
Create silastic collar (0.5–1 cm) and glue to exteriorised end, leaving 5 cm overhang

steps.title: Anesthetize and prepare animal
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 2.5 % isoflurane in oxygen (adjust as needed for maintenance). Apply eye lubricant, place the animal on a heated pad, shave and clean the ventral abdomen and dorsal neck.

substeps.instruction: Shave and clean ventral abdomen and dorsal neck

steps.title: Create ventral abdominal incision
steps.instruction: Make a ventral midline skin incision over the bladder region, place gauze dampened with sterile 0.9 % saline over the incision, and turn the animal onto its back.

steps.title: Create dorsal neck incision
steps.instruction: Make a dorsal midline skin incision at the base of the neck to serve as the exit site for the bladder cannula.

steps.title: Tunnel cannula subcutaneously
steps.instruction: Using hemostats, blunt‑dissect subcutaneously from the neck incision to the ventral abdominal incision, and gently pull the bladder cannula tubing through the tunnel.

steps.title: Create muscle incisions and tunnel cannula
steps.instruction: Incise the ventral abdominal muscle along the midline, then make a smaller secondary incision in the abdominal muscle on the same side as the tunneled tubing; feed the cannula through this opening into the abdominal cavity.

steps.title: Place purse‑string suture on bladder
steps.instruction: With cotton‑tipped applicators dampened with sterile 0.9 % saline, expose the bladder and place a very loose 4‑0 PDS purse‑string knot around the dome tip, positioned between one‑quarter and one‑third of the way down the apex; do not tighten.

steps.title: Pierce bladder dome
steps.instruction: Pierce the bladder dome tip with a 19 G needle, absorb any leaked urine with gauze, and enlarge the opening using fine forceps.

steps.title: Insert cannula into bladder
steps.instruction: Fill the cannula with 200–300 µl sterile saline, insert the flared end into the bladder so it lies below the purse‑string suture, then close and tie the purse‑string knot.

steps.title: Test for leaks and retie if needed
steps.instruction: Infuse 0.2 ml of 0.9 % sterile saline into the bladder to check for leaks; if leakage is observed, retie the purse‑string slightly lower than the original position.

steps.title: Close abdominal layers
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal muscle wall and skin using approved surgical closure procedures.

steps.title: Secure collar at neck
steps.instruction: At the dorsal neck, orient the collar and cannula tubing caudally, then place a suture through the neck skin, through the collar, and through the opposite side of the neck skin; tighten firmly. Repeat this two more times for a total of three securing sutures.

steps.title: Post‑operative analgesia and maintenance
steps.instruction: Administer postoperative analgesics and monitor the animal per institutional guidelines. To keep the cannula patent, infuse gentamicin (0.2 ml of 40 mg/ml in sterile 0.9 % saline) daily for 3 days, then continue daily infusions of sterile 0.9 % saline (0.5 ml).

steps.title: Habituate animal to recording chamber
steps.instruction: After recovery, habituate the animal to the recording chamber for 30 min per day for at least 3 days before cystometry recordings.

steps.title: Set up cystometry equipment
steps.instruction: Place the animal in the experiment chamber. Fill a 25 ml syringe with sterile 0.9 % saline and prime the pressure transducer and cannula line with sterile 0.9 % saline.

steps.title: Baseline pressure and saline infusion
steps.instruction: Set baseline pressure in LabChart by holding a flowing saline tube at transducer level before connecting to the cannula line; let it run for 1 minute, then connect to the animal. Infuse sterile 0.9 % saline into the bladder at 0.1 ml/min (or the rate required for the experiment). After line insertion, record bladder pressure for 30 min while the rat settles, then continue cystometry for an additional ~90 min (or the experiment’s required duration).

steps.title: Terminate recording and recover animal
steps.instruction: Turn off the pump, disconnect the cannula, and return the animal to its home cage for 2 hours.

steps.title: Perfuse for spinal cord IEG analysis
steps.instruction: Two hours after completing cystometry, anesthetize the animal and perform intra‑cardiac perfusion fixation; then dissect out the spinal cord for immediate‑early‑gene analysis (the 2‑hour interval allows gene expression).

steps.title: Seal exteriorised cannula end
steps.instruction: Seal the exteriorised end of the cannula with a blunt 25 G needle whose tip has been sealed with superglue.
